subtype: Partner unsure how to help during pregnancy [Receiver]
passage:
Week one: Kavitha had a list of baby names on the fridge and a head full of plans. Her partner Pallavi, twenty-one and newly pregnant, was asleep by eight, queasy most mornings and too tired to talk. When Kavitha sent her yet another article full of tips, Pallavi snapped, "Stop fixing me." Kavitha sat alone on the balcony, excited and oddly shut out.
Week three: Kavitha stopped sending tips. Each evening she asked, "What was hardest today?" and just listened. She took over the cooking and the laundry without being asked.
Week six: Kavitha went with Pallavi to the scan and held her hand when the heartbeat filled the room. Walking home, Pallavi leaned into her. "I felt so alone before. Now it feels like we're doing this together."

qa.q: What did Kavitha stick on the fridge?
qa.a: A list of baby names.

qa.q: How did Kavitha feel sitting alone on the balcony in week one?
qa.a: She felt excited but shut out, unsure of her place once her tips were rejected.

qa.q: What changed in week three, and why did it help?
qa.a: Kavitha stopped giving tips, listened each evening and took over cooking and laundry, which built closeness better than advice.

qa.q: How did the early weeks feel for Pallavi?
qa.a: She was queasy and exhausted, and the stream of tips made her feel fixed rather than supported, so she felt alone.

grounding: Shows a partner feeling excited and left out as pregnancy tiredness and nausea take over, and listening, chores and appointments building closeness.

subtype: Partner unsure how to help during pregnancy [Receiver]
passage: Vijay, you look lost since Rukhsana got pregnant. Let your Dadi Hafsa tell you about your grandfather. When I was carrying your father, I was sick every morning and asleep by sunset. Yusuf was so proud he told the whole mohalla, but at home he didn't know where to put himself. He'd say, "Eat more. Rest more. Don't lift that." Each piece of advice made me cry. One night he sat on the step outside, looking like a boy left out of a game. Then something changed. He stopped telling me what to do and started asking what I needed. He washed the clothes, much to his mother's shock. He came to every clinic visit and sat on the hard bench for hours. That's when we became a team, beta.

qa.q: What did Yusuf start doing that shocked his mother?
qa.a: He washed the clothes.

qa.q: How did Yusuf seem to feel sitting on the step outside?
qa.a: He felt left out and unsure, like a boy left out of a game, proud but not knowing how to help.

qa.q: What was the turning point in Dadi Hafsa's story, and why did it matter?
qa.a: Yusuf stopping the advice and asking what she needed, then sharing chores and going to clinic visits; it made them a team.

qa.q: How did Yusuf's early advice feel to young Hafsa?
qa.a: Sick and exhausted, she found each instruction upsetting enough to cry, rather than helpful.

grounding: Illustrates a partner who felt proud but left out during pregnancy discovering that listening, sharing chores and going to appointments help more than advice.

subtype: Partner unsure how to help during pregnancy [Receiver]
passage:
Antenatal clinic, counsellor's note, Tuesday
Thomas came in with Simran for her check-up and sat in the corner jiggling his leg. While she was with the midwife, he told me he felt useless. "She's sick every morning, exhausted, crying at adverts, and everything I suggest annoys her." He had been reading articles and giving her tips about food and sleep. He looked both excited and scared; he kept touching the scan photo in his wallet. We talked about how listening often helps more than advice, and about practical things he could take over: cooking, laundry, the water bottle by the bed at night. He said he had never come to an appointment before because he thought it was "her thing". He has booked the next three. When Simran came out, he asked her, "What would help this week?" and she smiled.

qa.q: What did Thomas keep touching?
qa.a: The scan photo in his wallet.

qa.q: How was Thomas feeling in the clinic?
qa.a: He felt useless, and both excited and scared, jiggling his leg in the corner.

qa.q: What did Thomas learn would help more than advice?
qa.a: Listening, taking over chores like cooking and laundry, and coming to the appointments.

qa.q: How might Simran feel when Thomas asks what would help?
qa.a: She seems pleased and closer to him, smiling at being asked rather than advised.

grounding: Shows a partner feeling excited, anxious and left out during a pregnancy, and learning that listening, chores and appointments help more than advice.

subtype: Partner unsure how to help during pregnancy [Receiver]
passage:
Thursday night
Aditi fell asleep at 8:30 again, mid-sentence. She's been throwing up most mornings, and today she cried because the pressure cooker whistle was "too loud". I made a joke. Wrong move.
Honestly, I don't know where I fit. I'm excited, I've got a name list on my phone, but I also feel like a spare part. Everyone asks her how she is. Nobody asks me. And every time I suggest something, ginger, a walk, an article, she looks at me like I'm the problem.
Today I tried something different. I didn't suggest anything. I just asked, "What's the worst part right now?" She talked for half an hour: the smells, the fear about the scan, her boss. I listened. Then I did the dishes and the laundry without being asked.
Next scan is on the 14th. I've taken the day off. I'm going.
Ujjwal

qa.q: When is the next scan?
qa.a: On the 14th.

qa.q: How has Ujjwal been feeling lately?
qa.a: Ujjwal feels excited but also left out, like a spare part, since everyone asks about Aditi and every suggestion seems wrong.

qa.q: What worked better than suggestions?
qa.a: Asking about the worst part and listening for half an hour, doing chores unasked, and planning to go to the scan.

qa.q: What is the pregnancy like for Aditi right now?
qa.a: She is exhausted and sick, sensitive to smells and noise, and scared about the scan and work.

grounding: Shows a partner feeling excited, anxious and left out in a pregnancy, and finding that listening and sharing chores build closeness better than advice.

subtype: Partner unsure how to help during pregnancy [Receiver]
passage: In their village near Thanjavur, Karthik felt like a spare part. Since Selvi's pregnancy began, her mother and aunts filled the house with advice, and Selvi was tired and sick every morning. When he offered suggestions from a video about food, she snapped, 'Everyone's telling me what to do!' He went out to the paddy field feeling useless and shut out, anxious too, though still excited about the baby. His uncle, watching him kick at the bund, said, 'Stop advising. Listen. Wash the vessels. Go with her to the clinic.' The next week Karthik swept the house before dawn, sat with Selvi through her worries without fixing them, and held the file at the health centre appointment. On the bus home she leaned on his shoulder.

qa.q: What did Karthik hold at the health centre appointment?
qa.a: The file.

qa.q: How did Karthik feel in the paddy field?
qa.a: He felt useless, shut out and anxious, even while excited about the baby.

qa.q: What helped Karthik grow closer to Selvi?
qa.a: Listening instead of advising, sharing chores like sweeping, and going to the appointment with her.

qa.q: How might Selvi have experienced Karthik's video advice?
qa.a: She probably felt overwhelmed and pressured, already tired and surrounded by everyone's instructions.

grounding: A young husband feels excited, anxious and left out during pregnancy and finds that listening, chores and appointments build closeness.
